extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary counsel, and attorneys responding to USPTO OED proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and factors governing practitioner conduct before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (duties to clients, fee handling, notification, cooperation with OED) and the procedural standards for service, default, and sanctions in OED disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication and timing for answer (37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When service cannot be accomplished pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a)(2)(i), the OED Director may serve by notice via publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b); notice via publication computes the time for filing an answer to be thirty days from the second publication of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure used here: Complaint published in Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks (Jan 28, 2014 and Feb 4, 2014); answer deadline moved from Dec 26, 2013 to March 4, 2014. If publications are properly made, the practitioner must file an answer within 30 days after second publication or risk default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default for failure to timely answer (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Failure to timely file an answer will constitute an admission of the allegations in the complaint and may result in default judgment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If practitioner does not file an answer after proper service, allegations are deemed admitted and Director's motion for default judgment may be granted (as in this case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to promptly pay or deliver client funds (37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall "promptly pay or deliver to the client as requested by a client the funds, securities, or other properties in possession of the practitioner which the client is entitled to receive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of violation: accepting USPTO filing fees from client and failing to remit them ($545.00 from Murray); failing to return unearned advance fees ($6,000 from Bradshaws); failing to return a client's patent application materials after request. Remedies include requiring return of funds and are an aggravating factor in sanctions analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty not to neglect legal matters (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not "neglect a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect includes failing to prepare, file, or prosecute patent applications and allowing client applications to become abandoned without client knowledge or consent (e.g., multiple clients' applications abandoned). Repeated neglect supports severe sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty not to misappropriate or fail to timely remit funds to the Office (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not "misappropriate or fail to properly or timely remit funds received by a practitioner ... from a client to pay a fee which the client is required by law to pay to the Office."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting money that included USPTO filing fees and failing to pay the Office (e.g., $545 and other filing-fee-inclusive advances) constitutes violation. The decision treats such failure as misappropriation/remittance violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify client of significant Office correspondence (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not "fail to inform a client ... of correspondence received from the Office ... when the correspondence (i) could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) is received by the practitioner on behalf of a client ..., and (iii) is correspondence of which a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances the client ... should be notified."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three-part test was applied repeatedly: Notices of Non-Compliant Amendments, Non-final Office Actions, Decisions on Petition, Notices to File Corrected Application Papers, and Notices of Abandonment all met the test. Failure to notify clients of such correspondence (and consequent abandonment) is a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to seek lawful objectives of a client (37 C.F.R. § 10.54(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not "fail to seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means permitted by law and the Disciplinary Rules."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglecting prosecution and allowing abandonment without seeking available legal means to protect client rights violates this duty (e.g., failing to revive applications, failing to respond to Office actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit, misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not "engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, and misrepresentation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misleading clients about status of applications (representing an application was filed when it was not), promising to return materials and failing to do so, and similar misrepresentations are violations and aggravating when deliberate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscription of intentionally or habitually violating USPTO Code (37 C.F.R. § 10.89(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation proscribes intentionally or habitually violating the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeatedly allowing client applications to become abandoned without notice or consent was treated as violating this provision and supports exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty not to violate or impede enforcement of USPTO Rules; duty to cooperate with OED (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.804(a) and 11.801(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(a): a practitioner shall not "violate or attempt to violate the USPTO Rules ..."; 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b): a practitioner shall not "fail ... to cooperate with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline in an investigation ... or knowingly fail to respond to a lawful demand or request for information ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to respond to OED RFIs and refusing to cooperate with investigation constitutes a violation under these provisions and aggravates sanction. The decision specifically finds violation of these duties after May 2, 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to update address with OED (37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner has an ongoing obligation to update his address with OED within thirty days of any change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to maintain current address can affect service and is noted as an issue; OED sent RFIs to an old address (returned) then located and sent to a new address. Practitioner still must report address changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions assessment factors (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Before sanctioning, the Court must consider: (1) whether practitioner violated a duty to client/public/legal system/profession; (2) whether practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused; (4) existence of aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court applied the four factors here, finding duties violated, intentional conduct, actual injury (monetary losses, abandoned IP), and multiple aggravating factors (substantial experience, pattern of misconduct) with no mitigating factors proved, supporting maximum sanction (exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner bears burden to raise mitigating circumstances (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.36(c), 11.49)
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden is on the practitioner to raise any affirmative defenses or mitigating circumstances and specify their nexus to the misconduct and any reason they may provide a defense or mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to appear and defend waives opportunity to contest state of mind or present mitigation. Absence of mitigating evidence supports heavier sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ABA Standards as guidance in sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court often looks to the American Bar Association Standards for Imposing Lawyer Sanctions when assessing attorney disciplinary sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ABA Standards inform analysis of aggravating/mitigating factors and proportionality of discipline; the decision cites ABA standards in support of exclusion given aggravation and lack of mitigation.
